name: vLLM bring-up of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8x RTX PRO 6000: 4584 tok/s prefill on the pure-torch eager fallback path at 1M context
model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (769B total, MXFP4 experts, Engram memory)
unit: tok/s prefill, eager mode, pure-torch logits path (NOT the optimized CUDA-graph production path)
methodology: AGGREGATE-IS-NOT-APPLICABLE: single-configuration prefill measurement from a 3-day bring-up, not a concurrency benchmark. Hardware: 8x RTX PRO 6000 96 GB (SM120, consumer Blackwell). Software fully pinned by the reporter: vLLM 0.1.dev20904 (deepseekv41-flash-0909 image), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, TP=8, --kv-cache-dtype fp8, --block-size 128, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85, 1M context enabled. CRITICAL CONDITION THAT DOMINATES THE NUMBER: the measurement is on the PURE-TORCH LOGITS PATH IN EAGER MODE, adopted because flashinfer sparse-MLA SM120 instantiations were missing for several (num_heads, topk) combinations. So this figure is a fallback-path number and must NOT be compared against an engine running CUDA graphs.
notes: Compare with care against [[ev-sglang-dsv41-production-128k-prefill-tps]], which reports 6,853 tok/s for the same model family on the same 8x RTX PRO 6000 hardware. SGLang is ~1.5x this figure, and the honest reading is that MOST of that gap is probably the eager-vs-CUDA-graph and pure-torch-vs-flashinfer difference rather than the schedulers - the vLLM reporter states the fallback was forced by missing SM120 flashinfer kernels, not chosen. Both numbers are third-party single-site field reports, neither is a vendor benchmark, and neither is an independent reproduction of the other. The same vLLM report contains the more important correctness finding, which is why the deployment value matters: the FP8 KV-cache block layout is '[64tok x 128B fp8 | 64tok x 4B fp32 scale]' (block-appended, not per-token interleaved), and misreading it 'passes short-prompt smoke tests and only fails at >=100K needle retrieval - silent numerical corruption'. Verification method published: a synthetic ~1M-token document with two facts inserted at 50% and 80% depth. VRAM note: ~91 GB of 96 GB per GPU, with Engram tables dominating (2 x ~100 GB shards = 189 GiB across the TP group).
